title: James McAvoy Reveals Which Film Paid Him “Bonkers” Residuals
full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All October 15, 2026 8:12pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source James McAvoy in 'Split.' Everett Collection James McAvoy is getting candid about pay, including which project paid him “bonkers” residuals. During a recent interview on the Happy Sad Confused podcast , the actor admitted that while his residual income typically isn’t consistent, he can’t say that about director M. Night Shyamalan ‘s 2016 film Split . “The only one that really consistently pays me is Split ,” he told host Josh Horowitz. “Well, I think it was made for like $6 million or something like that. And let’s say they spent $30 [million] advertising it, and in our first weekend, we made $40 [million].” Related Stories Business BBC Asks Judge to Force Trump to Sit for Deposition in His Own Lawsuit Against Broadcaster Movies Prepare to Fall in Love With 'Sense and Sensibility' Star Herbert Nordrum “So, we were in profit. So our first residual check came at the end of the first weekend. It was bonkers,” McAvoy added. Split follows three girls who try to escape after being kidnapped by a man (McAvoy) with a diagnosed 23 distinct personalities. He also reprised the role in 2016’s Glass . The Atonement actor went on to praise Shyamalan, saying he’s “super smart in so many ways.” “The thing that I took away from him was his preparedness because you know he made that film and Glass on incredibly modest budgets and was very focused,” he said, adding that the filmmaker maximized his shooting time by “being incredibly well-prepared” and “communicat[ing] with the crew.” While McAvoy has enjoyed the residuals from Split , he also admitted that he doesn’t “get too much money from [2008’s] Wanted .” “You’ve always got a good back end and there’s some in your contract, you get back end here and back end there. I very rarely see anything from anything,” he added. “You get the odd check for like a couple hundred quid here or sometimes you get checks for like 25 cents, and you’re like it literally costs more to post this than it did for me to check it.” THR

title: ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ Boss Meg Marinis on Texas Spinoff, Ellen Pompeo and Season 23 Premiere Cliffhangers
full_text: Skip to main content Ellen Pompeo in the season 23 premiere. Disney/Raymond Liu Logo text [This story contains some spoilers from the Grey’s Anatomy season 23 premiere, “Collide.”] Twenty-three seasons in and Grey’s Anatomy is not going anywhere. “No one has said anything to me about when the last season of Grey’s is going to be,” showrunner Meg Marinis tells The Hollywood Reporter when chatting about the new season, which returned Thursday night. That doesn’t mean she doesn’t ask. As the person charged with running ABC ‘s long-running, hit medical drama, Marinis wants to be prepared for whenever that day comes. “But it really seems like they want it to be a collaborative decision with Shonda,” she says of show creator Rhimes. “The series has done so much for the studio and network, they [would] want to do it right. And they’re not ready.” Related Stories TV 'DWTS' Pro Val Chmerkovskiy Apologizes to Carrie Ann Inaba for "Careless" Will Smith Oscars Slap Reference: "I Will Do Better" TV Where to Watch 'Grey's Anatomy' Season 23 Premiere They are in expansion mode, instead. Grey’s , whose previous spinoffs were Private Practice and Station 19 , is getting a new spinoff this 2026-2027 season that will be set at a rural West Texas medical center. Marinis co-created and is writing the untitled series with Rhimes, and Grey’s star/executive producer Ellen Pompeo is also exec producing the new show. “It’s related to Grey’s , but its stories are going to be different,” teases Marinis, who counts Texas as her home state. She’s always wanted to explore “what’s happening in medical deserts,” as well as “the disparity between people who can afford excellent healthcare and the people who can’t.” The latter comes up in the season 23 premiere of Grey’s , “Collide,” which welcomed Pompeo’s Meredith back to the hospital after the season 22 ending that sparked wedding bells for her and Nick (Scott Speedman). When Grey’s returned, one month had passed since the exits of beloved doctors Teddy (Kim Raver) and Owen (Kevin McKidd) , and the episode’s ending sets up more than enough threads to follow in coming weeks. Below, Marinis talks about all of it, including more on the spinoff, how she really feels about medical show competition (we’re looking at you, The Pitt ) and how much Pompeo will be on screen this season. *** Congrats on the news about the Grey’s spinoff ! We know that the series (which doesn’t yet have a name) will premiere sometime in the 2026-2027 season and that it’s set at a rural West Texas medical center — “the last chance for care before miles of nowhere.” You and Grey’s creator Shonda Rhimes are co-creating and writing the show, and Ellen Pompeo is executive producing. How has it been working on this second show amid the Grey’s schedule? ( Laughs .) I have a great team here at Grey’s that I lean on, and Shonda’s doing the new one with me so it’s easier when there’s two of us! Where are you in your work on the spinoff? Is there a timeline? We are working away. I can’t say much, but we’re far enough along where I’m really, really excited. We’re digging into the actual communities and true stories of what happens out in rural West Texas. There’s so much going on there that I haven’t seen on TV. I’m thrilled to be able to dive into that world. It’s so different from Grey’s . It’s related to Grey’s , but its stories are going to be different. Previous Grey’s spinoffs were Private Practice and Station 19 , but this feels a world away from Grey’s ‘ Seattle hospital. Were there lessons learned from those two shows that you are applying now? The only lessons are good lessons from those two. They were very successful spinoffs with hardcore fan followings. I loved both of them. This one is something dear to my heart [ Marinis is from Houston, Texas ] and being on a medical show like Grey’s , and hearing a lot about what’s happening in medical deserts, it’s hard to show that in Seattle. I’ve always been really interested in showing it, and in doing a small town show in Texas. Will Grey’s launch the Texas show in-show this season? We have thoughts based on airing schedule and things like that, but we’re still working it out, also because there are so many things going on on Grey’s , I want to make sure to do it where it’s servicing both shows equally. How do you view this within the larger Grey’s franchise? Does it signal anything about the flagship? It’s just expanding the flagship. No one has said anything to me about when the last season of Grey’s is going to be. I think it’s never! I always ask and they’re like, “Not now!” You always want to be prepared, as a showrunner of a season 23 show, that you’re aware of when that decision is going to happen. But it really seems like they want it to be a collaborative decision with Shonda. Because the series has done so much for the studio network, they want to do it right. And they’re not ready. We last spoke after last season’s finale and the exits of Kim Raver and Kevin McKidd’s Teddy and Owen, respectively, which you said was a difficult decision and related to the budget, which is something shows are experiencing across the industry. How did you approach season 23 with your very large ensemble? Will there be characters we see more or less of? Are you still feeling those constraints? Not yet. I mean, you always feel the general constraints of a large ensemble and what’s going on in the industry, so I’m mindful of how many times we go out on location and things like that. So the general constraints, yes. But no, those conversations usually are when they approach me later in the season — to drop that news on me! We’re in a positive place right now. On the show, the hospital is having some budget issues as well, but that’s mainly continuing on what we started last year about what’s happening to research funding and funding for healthcare in general. Now Grey Sloan is just feeling more of it. How much time has passed since the finale to start this premiere, and how is the hospital rebounding from losing veteran doctors, Teddy and Owen? It’s been about a month. We did that for a couple of reasons. I’ve done direct pickups for the past couple of seasons and I wanted to do something different, to start stories in different places. Also, I didn’t have Nick [Scott Speedman] available to me at the beginning of this season — he was left in the hospital in the finale, and he was busy on [his ABC show] R.J. Decker. That played into the decision. And I really wanted time for this VIP floor to come into play. We didn’t see that floor when we left the season last year. We don’t mention Teddy and Owen a ton in the premiere, because it’s been a month, and I didn’t want to start on such a down note. But we’re definitely feeling, and I’m feeling, the loss of Teddy and Owen. I’m searching for them in the scripts. We have to get a new chief. We don’t have a head of trauma right now. And it’s just leading to how busy the hospital is, maybe how our ER is not functioning as well as it should be. Winston [Anthony Hill] can do what he can, but he’s not a military trauma surgeon. James Wolk in the season 23 premiere. Disney/Ser Baffo James Wolk is a new character who was announced with a four-episode arc. Now we know his role — he’s the new chief. Will that arc extend? And how extensive was your search for the new chief? I love having him, but, you know, chiefs can come and go quickly on this show! But he’s a great character. He’s very fun to write for. He is also just a delightful human being and he seems to really enjoy his time here. We always have a long list of options [of actors] that people are sending us. He fit that suave look we wanted. He really seems like a villain you learn to love. Even when he’s being snarky about money, he’s still fascinating to watch. You say you got a long list of actors who want to come and play on Grey’s , a network show in its 23 rd season. How does that make you feel as showrunner about how appealing the show still is in the streaming era? It makes me feel great. I credit it to our show filming in L.A. If you have your family here, it’s really appealing to get to do an arc in L.A. I think there’s a reason we’re in season 23. It works, and I think a lot of people are fans of the show and curious about the show because it’s been going on for so long. And also, we’re really nice over here! People tell me all the time. Guest actors will write me emails and say, “This is the nicest set I’ve ever been on.” This episode had a line that Debbie Allen’s Catherine said to Ellen Pompeo, when she tells Meredith about hiring a new chief, “Well, you’re not here all the time” — which also could apply to Pompeo’s lesser onscreen role. Did those two have fun doing that scene? Yeah, they really enjoyed it! Sometimes we write stuff like that and we don’t even really think about it, and then when you watch it on set, you’re like, “I didn’t mean it that way!” ( Laughs .) But you know Debbie threw some sass into it and they were they were laughing; the two of them together laughed really hard. How much will we see Ellen Pompeo on screen this season? I ask you every year, but is it more or less? The same? [ Pompeo is also working as an EP on the Texas spinoff .] Like I say, every year, we take her as much as we can get. I know she has a couple of things going on in the mix, but we’re scheduling around that and she really lets me know ahead of time the days she is around, and it’s the same thing with Scott [Speedman]. It’s a logistics game, right? You want everybody to be able to do all their other projects, because work is work and it’s important right now to keep working in the industry. She and I have a good relationship. We’ll plan things out, and I’m more than happy to schedule around her. Will you be building towards Meredith and Nick’s wedding this season? We will definitely see Scott later in the season. In the premiere, we couldn’t work it out. But we’ll see Scott and we’ll definitely tag that engagement. So engagement , but you’re not confirming a wedding this season… [ Shrugs in coy silence .] Meredith’s storyline in this premiere highlights the upstairs-downstairs of Grey Sloan. Meredith is fighting back against tiered treatment and Catherine is approaching this as a plan to help with their financials. How is this a larger story you want to tell this season, and why did that interest Ellen for this to be Meredith’s fight, at least for now? I’m interested in telling that story because I’m seeing it so much now across healthcare. The disparity is growing even wider between people who can afford excellent healthcare and the people who can’t. I think it’s also really interesting because, historically, Grey Sloan has always provided VIP care, the way we’ve told it on the show. So now, are they dividing care into tiers? A lot of our doctors are going to question it. But these floors are popping up all over the country. Obviously, they’ve had them in L.A. for a while, but also in New York, and even when I went to see my dad and Houston. When he had pneumonia, there was a VIP floor there. I saw the signs and I was like, “What’s the difference between what my dad’s getting and what they’re getting?” I find it fascinating. There are a lot of stories where sometimes you don’t want to be on the VIP floor because they don’t have all the tools you need if something catastrophic happens. But also, if I had a very chronically ill family member and I had the means, why wouldn’t I throw every dollar I had at helping? It’s an interesting debate to sink our teeth into. Meredith, especially, is an owner of the hospital, so she understands the business. But her whole career, she has fought for the have-nots. So it’s like, do you keep the hospital doors open? What side do you choose? Will Ellen be appearing in batches, like a five-episode arc to tell storylines? Or will she pop in and out in a less structured way? I would love for it to be structured like that, but schedules aren’t working! ( Laughs .) But there are runs where she’s in for more than one episode. Do you have an episode count for her this season? Not yet. Are there any other returns you can tease? Probably not. Obviously, she’s been in the picture, so people know that Jen Landon is returning [as Toni]. But as for old cast series regulars, I can’t tease any of that right now. The Grey’s social account teased a Cristina Yang (Sandra Oh) return, and the fans went wild. They were speculating Yang would maybe come back for Meredith’s wedding to Nick. Anything you can say about that? She is welcome to walk in these doors anytime! I would love for her to. At one point, she was doing some theater in London, but it would be a dream come true to have her back. You also kicked this season off with a classic disaster episode, and one that picks up on a lot of relationship threads that were unfinished at the end of last season, taking a backseat to Teddy and Owen’s big goodbye. Did this premiere feel more nostalgic to you — chaos and romance? You’re right that a lot of stories had to take up smaller real estate in the last couple of episodes at the end of last season, rightfully so, because we were writing off two long-term, beloved characters. I love when people have relationship issues with each other, and you have to throw them on a medical case together. There’s nothing more Grey’s than that. I love all those looks between Amelia and Toni and them having to come together; and Simone [Alexis Floyd] and Lucas [Niko Terho] and West [Trevor Jackson]; Jules [Adelaide Kane] and Winston having to operate with Bailey (Chandra Wilson). It’s quintessential Grey’s when there’s the bubbling underneath it as they’re trying to save someone’s life. Caterina Scorsone and Jen Landon as Amelia and Toni in the season 23 premiere. Disney/Raymond Liu You have a pregnancy reveal at the end of this premiere with Simone. We do. Grey’s has tackled pregnancy and abortion storylines before. How will this one be different? It is different. We’ve never done it this way before. It’s going to take a couple of episodes to play out. I also think this one is different because Simone was just told that she probably wouldn’t be able to have children; to be able to conceive and get pregnant. So that’s going to be top of mind for her. That’s a struggle. She’s someone who’s put career first and she’s worked really hard to get where she is. I think that’s what a lot of us struggle with, right? Do you put the career on pause for a second and start a family? It’s something so many people relate to, so we’ll show that. But it is different. We’ve never done it this way before. The other bomb at the end of the premiere is Jo (Camilla Luddington) quitting the hospital, as Link (Chris Carmack) is still being secretive about his pills. This couple is always tested! I know, what can I do? I love torturing them! Sometimes they’ll be like, “ Really ?!” They have such talent to play funny stories, and we played them very light and funny for a long time. Then I kind of tapped into this talent that I did not know they both had, and it’s amazing to watch. Their performances are so great. Even Jo watching that thing in the elevator? Camilla’s performance is exquisite. So yeah — we’re putting them through it again. ( Laughs .) Blue got fired at the end of last season, and now Harry Shum Jr. is on Dancing With the Stars . Did he come to you for approval to be on that series, and is that impacting his story and all? Obviously, he’s back as a series regular. It did not impact his story. It just happened to be that he was the character who was quitting, and then he, ABC and his team came to me after and I was like, “Oh, this really worked out, because now people are going to think once he’s announced on DWTS that maybe we went through with [firing him off the show].” But I think there’s been so much social media of him in his scrubs that his return is spoiled! We’re so happy for him. He’s so talented. A lot of us have gotten to go see the live taping of DWTS . You’ll see him and Jenna Johnson just rehearsing outside in between setups for Grey’s . On Tuesdays, Harry’s not here because Dancing With the Stars films. But other than Tuesdays, he’s really been able to schedule rehearsals around the show. I’m sure he’s exhausted! Grey’s remains the longest-running medical drama on TV. But more medical shows are popping up on streaming; there’s The Pitt. You could compare that to ER , which was on at the beginning of Grey’s . Does that sharpen what you’re trying to do? Do you ever worry about overlap? How do you feel about medical show competition? I don’t worry too much about it because I feel like what’s good for one medical show is good for all. It’s trending again. Anytime that it can trend, I think it’s a great thing. We’re so different than The Pitt that I don’t worry about that one. I was a huge ER fan. It had a huge influence on me wanting to be a TV writer. I love medical shows. I love the better ones more. ( Laughs .) And then I’m excited to introduce this new [the Texas spinoff] into the fold. Grey’s is a streaming show too now, on Netflix, courting new generations of viewers. But 23 seasons in, what are your tricks to keeping the show fresh and keeping the cast engaged? It has been a long time and it can be difficult. It can be tricky, but I also think that medicine has changed so much and the world has changed so much. Between AI and climate change and where money goes toward research, there are always new things that we haven’t explored. Often, we have an overwhelming amount of stories we want to tell and we don’t get to tell all of them, so we have a huge bank of things we’re interested in. Also, knowing that we have a 23-year history of characters who have come and gone and bringing them back. And, you can always introduce new interns! You have three series originals stars who are still on the show: Ellen, Chandra Wilson and James Pickens Jr. Are you never letting them go? Yes, I will say, I am never letting those three go! I mean, I hope they never go. It’s not gonna be me who writes it! *** Grey’s Anatomy releases new episodes Thursdays at 10 p.m. on ABC, releasing on Hulu the next day. THR

title: Daisy Edgar-Jones Reveals She Might Be “Slightly Deaf” in One Ear After Filming ‘Twisters’
full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All October 15, 2026 6:58pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Daisy Edgar-Jones in 'Twisters.' Everett Collection Twisters has had a lasting impact on Daisy Edgar-Jones , but not necessarily in the way that she wanted. During a recent episode of Jake Shane ‘s Therapuss podcast , the actress revealed that she might be “slightly deaf” in one ear after shooting the 2024 action-adventure thriller, directed by Lee Isaac Chung. “I think I still am slightly deaf in my left ear because there was so much debris and wind that was entering from a sharp left,” she said. “It was a windy shoot. It was quite ironic because we were shooting in Oklahoma and often would have to shut down filming because of an actual wind storm, to then recreate a wind storm once it’s passed. It was a wild experience.” Related Stories Movies 'Street Fighter' Eyes Box Office Victory as Buzzy Elizabeth Holmes Doc Heads for Strong Launch Movies Prepare to Fall in Love With 'Sense and Sensibility' Star Herbert Nordrum Twisters , which served as a standalone sequel, came nearly two decades after 1996’s Twister . The film followed Kate Carter (Edgar-Jones), a retired tornado-chaser and meteorologist who is persuaded to return to Oklahoma to work with a new team and new technologies. There, she meets Tyler Owens (played by Glen Powell), a content creator who posts his storm-chasing adventures. The Sense and Sensibility star definitely wasn’t afraid to get in on the action, previously telling The Hollywood Reporter that she got “a bit addicted” to doing stunts after filming Twisters . “It was so stunt heavy and I’d never done really proper stunts, so I was so curious to see how they were going to achieve a lot of the action sequences, but I’m a bit addicted now, I’ve got the bug,” Edgar-Jones said in 2024. “It was so much fun. I mean we had a phenomenal stunt department who really just helped to immerse us in it, also keep us safe. Most of the stunts were sort of being battered by wind, rain and debris so it was definitely an interesting filming experience.” THR

title: ‘SNL’ Star Michael Che Reacts to Shane Gillis’ Controversial Monologue: “That’s Comedy”
full_text: Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All October 15, 2026 6:27pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Michael Che Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images Logo text Michael Che has been preparing for potential questions about Shane Gillis’ controversial monologue on Saturday Night Live last weekend, and the moment has arrived. “I gotta do more press this week to promote the special. Wonder what every fucking question’s gonna be about,” Che wrote on his Instagram earlier this week, regarding the press tour for his new Netflix stand-up special, Michael Che: Shot in Minnesota . “Thanks a lot Shane.” For context, after hosting the NBC sketch comedy program on Saturday, Gillis drew heat over his joke about women working out. Related Stories TV Druski Becomes First Online Creator to Host 'SNL' TV Former 'SNL' Star Ego Nwodim Reacts to Shane Gillis' Controversial Joke About Women “I haven’t been to the gym in so long, I didn’t know women just dress like whores now,” Gillis said to the live audience. “Look, I’m sorry, there’s no other way to describe [it]. Have you seen it? I’ve seen it. The shorts? Have you seen the shorts? They’re neon, like, artificial bait-colored? And the wrinkles go around the cheeks and all combine at the butthole. And don’t look. You’re not allowed to look. For real, don’t look, because they are filming. I’m in the background of like 10 TikToks right now.” Despite being adamant about not being interested in weighing in on the discourse, Che, who anchors “Weekend Update” with Colin Jost on SNL , was asked on the Today show Thursday about the controversy. “That’s comedy,” he said. “It’s like, you think it’s funny and some people don’t.” He was later asked if he laughed at Gillis’ joke about women, to which Che replied, “I was at cue cards actually, thinking about what I was gonna say that was gonna make people upset. I didn’t even see it until the next day.” Che isn’t a stranger to controversial jokes, especially during his bi-annual joke swap with Jost on SNL , where the jokes can get quite dicey. “That’s why I can’t criticize anybody for swinging and missing because I’ve definitely swung and missed too,” the comedian said on Today . “I try to keep that heat off of me.” After drawing some backlash for his remarks on the NBC morning program, Che responded to a fan on Instagram who asked why he had no problem calling Kanye “Ye” West out in the past, but not Gillis. “That’s a fair question. Especially since when I called Kanye out, I did so privately. I had no idea he was filming. Point being, when I have a problem with someone I address them in person. Not thru the media. I’m not gonna drag someone on the Today show, when I can just text them. It’s a courtesy that’s been extended to me in the past, and I like to pay that forward.” Following Gillis’ monologue, Dan Levy was among some celebrities who slammed the comedian over his joke about women at the gym. “Women wearing short shorts at the gym does not make them whores. It makes the men calling them whores misogynists. There’s a difference there,” the Schitt’s Creek co-creator and star wrote in part. Levy added in his Instagram post, “I’m speechless that something like that can exist on live national television. And to be perfectly honest, more men need to be standing up in opposition to it because it’s complacency that has created the environment in which women are sexually assaulted and it’s a ‘conversation’ as opposed to a ‘crime.’” Former SNL castmember Ego Nwodim also responded with a photo of herself at the gym with the caption, “Whore reporting for duty.” THR

title: ‘DWTS’ Pro Val Chmerkovskiy Apologizes to Carrie Ann Inaba for “Careless” Will Smith Oscars Slap Reference: “I Will Do Better”
full_text: Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All October 15, 2026 6:18pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Val Chmerkovskiy and Carrie Ann Inaba. Ethan Miller/Getty Images, Disney/Eric McCandless Logo text Dancing With the Stars professional dancer Val Chmerkovskiy has apologized to Carrie Ann Inaba for his “careless” reference to Will Smith’s infamous Oscars slap in a since-deleted TikTok Story post. “I want to apologize from the bottom of my heart for my recent post,” the pro wrote on his Instagram Story Thursday. “I have reached out to Carrie Ann to apologize directly and personally, and I also want to apologize publicly as I understand my words affect so many outside of our internal DWTS family. I should have never made the reference that I did and I deeply regret it. I recognize that I am in a fortunate position to have a platform and to be a role model to some, and I need to treat that with more care by actively pausing to think before I post to ensure what I am sharing aligns with who I am, and who I want to be for you all.” Related Stories TV 'DWTS': Val Chmerkovskiy References Will Smith's Oscars Slap While Defending Wife Jenna Johnson Amid Carrie Ann Inaba Criticism TV Justin Baldoni Makes Rare Public Appearance on 'Dancing With the Stars' Following Blake Lively Legal Battle Chmerkovskiy concluded, “I am truly sorry to Carrie Ann, and everyone who I hurt with my careless post. I will do better moving forward.” The three-time DWTS winner had been defending his wife, fellow pro Jenna Johnson, online following criticism the judge shared for her samba performance with Harry Shum Jr. on Tuesday’s Super Bowl Night. Chmerkovskiy particularly received backlash for a TikTok Story he posted on Wednesday that read, “You almost saw Fresh Prince enter the ballroom last night,” a comment many took as a reference to Smith slapping Chris Rock at the 2022 Oscars. Inaba responded to his remarks earlier on Instagram Thursday, writing “So this is what we are doing now?” while resharing a screenshot of a Page Six post featuring the dancer’s “Fresh Prince” comment, alongside a split image of Smith and Chmerkovskiy. After Johnson and her celebrity partner Harry Shum Jr. performed a samba to Usher’s “Yeah!,” the judge told the mirrorball champion, “I think you need to put more content in your dances. Especially because [Harry’s] so good, I want to see you challenge yourself a little bit more in the vein of what we’re looking for. And there was a lift.” Johnson responded to Inaba’s comments by asking, “A lift?” Inaba brought out a piece of paper with the definition of lift, which she read during the live episode: “A lift is — I just need to say it — any movement during which one of the dancers has both feet off the floor at the same time with the assistance or support of their partner. Yeah, lift.” Chmerkovskiy’s Fresh Prince TikTok Story was posted on Wednesday and was live for at least six hours. One Reddit thread was flooded with theories that Chmerkovskiy’s post was “likely referring to when Will Smith slapped Chris Rock for making a comment about his wife,” adding that they took his comment as he allegedly “wanted to slap Carrie Ann for telling Jenna to step it up.” The story was subsequently deleted. Smith walked onto the Oscars stage while Rock was hosting in 2022 after he made a joke about his wife, Jada Pinkett Smith, starring in a G.I. Jane sequel. “Keep my wife’s name out of your fucking mouth!” Smith infamously yelled from the crowd after he returned to his seat following the slap. THR

title: ‘Street Fighter’ Eyes Box Office Victory as Buzzy Elizabeth Holmes Doc Heads for Strong Launch
full_text: × Skip to main content By Ryan Gajewski Plus Icon Ryan Gajewski Senior Entertainment Reporter View All October 15, 2026 5:27pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Callina Liang in 'Street Fighter.' Paramount Pictures Logo text Street Fighter is hoping for a muscular opening weekend at the box office as it faces competition from a number of newcomers, including A24’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything . Paramount Pictures releases video game adaptation Street Fighter in more than 3,500 North American theaters on Friday, with the studio projecting a range of mid-$30 millions domestically and another sum of mid-$30 millions internationally. Director Kitao Sakurai’s feature carries an $82 million production budget that is split evenly between producers Legendary Pictures and Capcom . Paramount sees only upside for the film that marks the first release in its distribution deal with Legendary. Related Stories Movies Ben Affleck Warns 'Digger' Box Office Bomb Will Lead to "A Bunch of Sh***y Homogenized Movies" Movies Prepare to Fall in Love With 'Sense and Sensibility' Star Herbert Nordrum Critics have not been blown away, with Street Fighter holding a 43 percent approval rating from reviewers on Rotten Tomatoes. In his review for The Hollywood Reporter , critic Frank Scheck called the film a “jumbled tonal mess” and “only sporadically entertaining.” Noah Centineo , Andrew Koji and Callina Liang star in the movie that centers on a combat tournament. Street Fighter marks the third feature in the franchise adapting the Capcom video game that launched in 1987. Austin Abrams in Whalefall . 20th Century Studios Also hitting theaters is Whalefall , with 20th Century Studios releasing director Brian Duffield’s survival thriller in 3,065 North American locations. The studio projects an opening between $10 million and $12 million for the $60 million-budgeted feature that adapts author Daniel Kraus’ 2023 novel. After leading last month’s Resident Evil , Austin Abrams stars as a scuba diver who, while searching for the remains of his late father (Josh Brolin), is swallowed by a sperm whale. Whalefall holds a 70 percent critics approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. In his review , THR chief film critic David Rooney wrote that the movie is “just not batshit crazy enough to be much fun.” You Can See Everything A24 A24 has high hopes for You Can See Everything , the documentary following infamous Theranos founder Holmes in the lead-up to the start of her prison sentence. The studio releases the feature in around 800 North American theaters, with projections coming in around $7 million for the $5 million-budgeted doc from directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim . Earlier this year, Melania opened to $7 million from 1,700 domestic theaters, marking the highest-grossing non-music doc launch in over a decade. You Can See Everything boasts a superlative 100 percent critics score on Rotten Tomatoes. In her review for THR , critic Angie Han deems it “smart, funny and full of surprises.” Daisy Edgar-Jones in Sense and Sensibility . Courtesy of Focus Features Also making its debut this weekend is Focus Features’ Sense and Sensibilit y, which opens in 2,436 North American locations. Focus projects an $8 million domestic haul for filmmaker Georgia Oakley’s adaptation of Jane Austen’s classic work, with the movie carrying a budget in the mid-$20 millions. Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles star as the Dashwood sisters as they grapple with their father’s death. Ang Lee helmed 1995’s Oscar-winning version that starred Emma Thompson and remains well-regarded. The new Sense and Sensibility stands at 77 approval from reviewers on Rotten Tomatoes. Rooney writes that the film “seldom steps out from the long shadow of Ang Lee’s enchanting 1995 retelling.” THR

title: Ben Affleck Warns ‘Digger’ Box Office Bomb Will Lead to “A Bunch of Sh***y Homogenized Movies”
full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All October 15, 2026 5:18pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ben Affleck waves during the red carpet and fan event of the movie 'Animals' at Centro Comercial Mitikah. Toya Sarno Jordan/Getty Images Logo text Amid Digger ‘s box office bomb, Ben Affleck is warning that those who are celebrating the film’s poor performance could instead lead to “a bunch of shitty homogenized movies.” During an appearance on the Happy Sad Confused podcast this Monday, the Animals actor addressed the poor performance of Tom Cruise ‘s latest movie. He argued that criticizing a “big swing” movie could result in studios later opting to take a safer approach with future projects. “It’s a little bit like the high-school bullying thing, with people who hadn’t even seen movies. You see it happening now, frankly, with Digger . Everybody wants to celebrate this bomb as if it’s the most exciting thing to happen, and you think like, it’s a pretty ambitious, interesting movie made by interesting people that have talent,” Affleck said. Related Stories Movies Ben Affleck Calls Filming 'Justice League' a "Low Point" in His Career: "About as Gross as It Gets" Movies Theo James, Hoyeon, Christian Slater Thriller 'The Hole' Lands Summer 2027 Release From Orion (Exclusive) “Everybody wants to count the money, what it lost or whatever. To me, I just think, like, if you punish movies that take risks, guess what you’re going to get? A bunch of shitty, homogenized movies,” he explained. “You cannot do something interesting without taking a big swing, and that means you’re going to sometimes look bad.” In The Hollywood Reporter ‘s review of Digger , chief film critic David Rooney wrote, “ Digger is basically what happens when you put two outsize egos together with nobody holding the reins to keep their most self-indulgent impulses in check. Piloted by a spectacularly obnoxious Tom Cruise, who evidently spent hours in the makeup chair each day to look his age, Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s wannabe Dr. Strangelove is a heavy-handed cataclysm scenario built around the blunt point that any attempt to halt global warming this late in the game is pure political theater.” Digger opened with $8 million domestically, totaling $12 million internationally. The film’s box office performance has sparked many conversations and led to many celebrities speaking out in support of the movie directed by Alejandro G. Iñárritu. Among those were Anne Hathaway , who topped Digger at the box office with Verity in their opening weekends, giving the film a perfect score. She wrote on Letterboxd, “I loved this brilliant movie. It’s smart and trippy and aggressive and funny and ambitious. It’s worth making the time see and decide for yourself what you make of it. For me? 10/10.” THR

full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Kylie Minogue, Jonathan Groff & Catherine Tate Join ‘Bad Fairies’ Cast With Cynthia Erivo ‘The Beekeeper 2’ Teaser: Jason Statham Kicks Rogue Govt. Robert Voets/Warner Bros./Christopher Polk/Deadline Six years after announcing her departure from CBS ‘s Mom , Anna Faris has reacted to Chuck Lorre ‘s comments about her exit. On Thursday, the actress shared a statement explaining that she “never took a day of [the show] for granted” after series co-creator Lorre wrote in his new memoir Sitcom that he “was, in fact, correct” about his initial reluctance to cast her as Christy Plunkett in the sitcom. Related Stories Books Chuck Lorre Q&A On The Care & Feeding Of Sitcom Stars & Why A WGA Strike Doomed Democracy Casting ‘Mom’ Star Anna Faris Exits CBS Comedy Series After Seven Seasons “Yikes. Yes, I read a few things. I really didn’t see that coming. Of course it hurts,” she began in a statement on Instagram . “Chuck gave me a job I loved, and for seven years I never took a day of it for granted. I’m proud of what we made together, and nothing changes how grateful I am for those people and those years.” Faris continued: “I’ve been sober for a year and a half. I was on a show about recovery, and then I lived it. Now I’m healthy, I’m working, and I’m happier than I’ve been in a long time. If anyone reading this is where I was, I hope that’s useful. It gets better. I’m proof.” Watch on Deadline Premiering in 2013, Faris starred in the first seven seasons of Mom as Christy, a recovering alcoholic who struggles to maintain a job, her family and her sobriety as her mom Bonnie (Allison Janney), who’s also in recovery, moves in with her. View this post on Instagram Faris left the show in 2020 to “pursue new opportunities,” leaving Janney as the sole lead for the eighth and final season, which ended in 2021. In an excerpt from Sitcom , Lorre wrote: “I wasn’t sure Anna would be appropriate for this kind of material. Then I thought about how badly I’d bungled my working relationship with Charlie Sheen.” After his experience with Charlie Sheen on Two and a Half Men , Lorre recalled conceding, “Someone’s personal life is none of my business. The mom in Mom would be, and should be, Anna Faris.” Lorre added: “As the years went by, it became apparent that my initial reluctance to hire Anna was, in fact, correct. title: ‘Law & Order’ Season 26, Episode 2 Recap: What Happened To Det. Vincent Riley In Reid Scott’s Final Episode?
full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando ‘Law & Order’ Season 26, Episode 2 Recap: What Happened To Det. Vincent Riley In Reid Scott’s Final Episode? Aaron Paul Mourns ‘Breaking Bad’ Co-Star RJ Mitte: “I Am So Sorry You Were Hurting, My Friend” Aaron Sorkin On ‘The West Wing’ Revival: “It Would Be Very, Very Tricky To Do In The Current Environment” View All October 15, 2026 8:00pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Reid Scott NBC SPOILER ALERT: This post contains details on Law & Order Season 26, Episode 2, which aired on NBC on Thursday, October 15. Earlier this year, Deadline reported that Reid Scott , who plays Senior Detective Vincent Riley, was leaving the NBC procedural. Scott’s exit finally aired in the second episode of Season 26 titled “Into the Mystic.” The episode opens with Riley sitting at his work desk, and something prompts him to look for Ray Biller. When he arrives at Ray’s apartment, the person who answers the door says Ray isn’t there. Riley orders the guy to call Ray to find out where he is. Related Stories News 'Newlyweds': Bruce Helford Tapped As New Showrunner In 'Anything But Love' Reunion With Jamie Lee Curtis, Production Hiatus Extended News 'Friends' Returning To Channel 4 After 15 Years Moments later, Riley calls Nolan Price (Hugh Dancy) and tells him, “Need to talk to you right away. Call me back.” Watch on Deadline Riley then calls Theo Walker (David Ajala) and tells him he’s headed to a bar as “something is cooking.” After heading to the bar, Riley gets a text from Walker saying he’s on his way. As Riley approaches the bar, he notices Ray exiting the establishment. Riley follows Ray, who tells him he needs to talk. However, when he turns around, he shoots Riley twice in the chest and runs off. Walker arrives at the scene and notices a man running away with a gun in hand. However, by the bar, there’s a lot of commotion as Riley bleeds from the gunshot wounds. Walker calls for help, applies pressure, and yells, “Vince, stay with me, come on!” Lieutenant Jessica Brady (Maura Tierney) arrives at the hospital, and Walker fills her in on what happened, leaving her shocked and without words. At the hospital, the doctor tells Walker they couldn’t save Riley, leaving all his colleagues in despair. Robert Calvino, played by James Badge Dale, is introduced to help investigate Riley’s death. Riley’s wife shows up at the police station and tells them that he had been withdrawing “lots of cash” recently. Although Riley’s wife didn’t know what the money was for, she did note that he was a drinker. Jessica Brady and Robert Calvino visit a woman who Riley had been arguing with hours earlier on the day that he died. The pregnant woman tells officers that Riley was giving her cash as he “felt guilty” for killing her husband years before. Brady and Calvino find out Riley was at Ray Biller’s apartment and talk to his friend, who corroborates what Riley was doing there the night he was killed. When they get back to the office, Nolan tells them that Ray Biller’s brother, Wayne, whom he found for murder, was killed in prison. The police find Ray Biller, who was attending his brother’s Wayne funeral, and arrest him as the prime suspect in Riley’s death. Actor Ryan Eggold made an appearance reprising his role as Matt Riley, the troubled brother of Detective Vincent Riley, showing up in court and wanting justice for his brother’s death. The prosecution runs into a problem when Ray Biller’s defense argues that they can’t prove he was the one who killed Riley, as they didn’t recover a weapon. DA Nicholas Baxter (Tony Goldwyn) is determined to put Walker on the stand, but Nolan pushes back as he doesn’t believe Walker actually saw Ray Biller as the man who killed Riley. On the day of the verdict, Ray Biller was found guilty on the charge of first-degree murder. Although it was a victory for the prosecution, doubt remains over whether Walker told the truth, and Nolan remains skeptical about whether they did the right thing. In July, Deadline first reported that Reid Scott was leaving Law & Order , after joining in Season 23. He reportedly decided to exit the NBC procedural due to the strain of the cross-country commute to New York City, where the series is filmed. Shaken up by the experience, Meredith proposed to Nick while he was lying in his hospital bed, a throwback to their first meeting when Nick was admitted to Grey Sloan with a failing kidney in Season 14. He said yes, an answer he apparently had had ready since that fateful first encounter. Watch on Deadline In another Grey’s tradition, the finale also included a jaw-dropping WTF moment. Toni (Jen Landon), after some soul-searching over her ex-wife’s appeal to get back together, went to Amelia’s (Caterina Scorsone) apartment to tell her that she had broken it off with her ex and was falling in love with her only to find out that Amelia had hooked up with Cass (Sophia Bush). (Cass had popped in at Grey Sloan earlier in the day to help with the influx of patients from the bridge collapse.) In other developments, Kwan (Harry Shum Jr.) is still fired. He tried to get back on Richard’s (James Pickens Jr.) good graces by helping with injured patients but that didn’t work. New couple Winston and Jules’ secret relationship is no more (secret) after they were intercepted sneaking out of an on-call room by Ben (Jason George), a newly minted plastics fellow. New mom Jo (Camilla Luddington) is facing an existential crisis and may not be a doctor anymore while her supportive husband Link’s (Chris Carmack) dependance on painkillers is becoming worrisome. Bailey, defying her suspension to help save Nick, is considering a career change of her own as she plans to go for a Masters in public health. And the Simone (Alexis Floyd)-Lucas (Nike Terho)-Wes (Trevor Jackson) love triangle, which had been dormant for most of the season, came back in full force after Simone and Lucas slept together and Wes asked her to go steady. Below, Grey’s Anatomy executive producer/showrunner Meg Marinis is breaking down all non-Owen & Teddy developments in the finale and how they would carry over to Season 23, including potential other cast departures and Speedman’s status as his ABC series R.J. Decker is yet to be renewed (but is looking good). For her explanation of McKidd and Kim Raver’s exit and the reasons behind it, r ead Part 1 of Deadline’s interview . ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ (L-R): Scott Speedman as Nick, Ellen Pompeo as Meredith in Season 14. ABC Meredith & Nick: Meet Cute Redo DEADLINE: Meredith and Nick recreated their first encounter for the surprise proposal. How did you settle on that and why did she pop the question? MARINIS : Well, Meredith has always been pretty clear that she didn’t want to get married again after Derek. In truth, she didn’t really want to get married to Derek, they did that in the end because of trying to make sure that they could have the best chances at adopting Zola. And so I think marriage is not something that is ingrained in her, but clearly, when she heard the story of how he wanted to get married in the middle of the season, when his sister came to visit, and how his sister had taken away this happy life from him, I think that got put in the back of her mind that that is something that he’d always wanted, but he’s such a nice guy, he loves her so much that he’s never going to force her to do anything, especially since she had such a painful ending to her first marriage. I think she’s also scared that if she ever got married again, what if she lost him like it happened with Derek? And I think when she realized that you’re going to have that fear no matter what, why not do it? I told Ellen at the beginning of this season, I was like, I want to end with a proposal. And she was like, ‘Agh’. I was like, I do, I do. So it was something that I’ve been planning since the beginning of the season, and it was very seeded with that middle episode between the two of them. I obviously don’t know the fate of R.J. Decker. I haven’t heard anything. And so it was a very small window that we got Scott to come and film in L.A. and so it worked out that, okay, if we can get him in a hospital bed and put him on the table, then we can utilize as much time with Scott that we had. It was kind of a perfect scenario. DEADLINE: You took a leap of fate with the proposal not knowing whether the actor playing the groom-to-be would be available next season. Will it depend on R.J. Decker’ s fate how much we will see of Scott on Grey’s next year? MARINIS : For sure, it will depend on if R.J. Decker goes, and I hope it does for Scott. But he was so game, he flew in on a Friday, we filmed on a Saturday, and we worked it out. He was being part of the Grey’s family. And so we’ll just have to figure out if we can plan in advance with the other show and work it out again. DEADLINE: Are you planning a big wedding? We know Meredith is not keen on the idea but a wedding would bring people back. We haven’t seen many Grey’s alumni for awhile; I feel this season was one of the lightest in terms of cast returns. MARINIS : You know, I don’t, it all really kind of depends on Scott’s schedule and what we decide creatively. I do not think Meredith is a big wedding person, but we’ll just have to see. DEADLINE: And in terms of returns, was it intentional that you had fewer people coming back vs previous seasons? MARINIS : No. When we realized that we needed to exit two characters we wanted to spend the most time on the characters that we have currently. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’: Harry Shum Jr. as Kwan (Blue) Disney/Anne Marie Fox Ben & Kwan: One Rising & One Leaving? DEADLINE: We know about Kim Raver and Kevin McKidd but are other cast members leaving too? For example, Harry Shum Jr. whose character Kwan was fired twice in the last two episodes? MARINIS : His fate is still undecided. Blue is scared out of his mind, so we’ll just have to see when we come back in the fall. He doesn’t have a job at Grey Sloan right now, so we’ll have to see what happens to him. DEADLINE: There was this interesting look on Catherine’s face when Richard kicked Blue out in the finale. It felt like she was persuadable. MARINIS: It’s kind of a different shade on Catherine, it’s nice. DEADLINE: But to reiterate, of the series regulars, no one except Kevin and Kim are leaving, right? MARINIS : We’ll always have to wait to see who shows up in Season 23. DEADLINE: We’ve talked about Ben floating around, trying to find himself since returning to Grey Sloan. He just got this fellowship; has he now settled? MARINIS : I think he’s as settled as Ben Warren can be. But yes, I’m interested in seeing him follow this fellowship and wear those navy scrubs and be looked at someone who has authority now. That was really important to me this season, to bring him out of Bailey’s shadow, to give him a mentor who doesn’t also see him as someone who’s had a bunch of different jobs. She’s just meeting him for the first time as Ben Warren, someone who’s interested in plastics, and so she doesn’t know all the history necessarily. And I think he really is proving himself. I think that was a really powerful story in Episode 17 last week for him, where he saved Maya. He did great work and saved your life and he really deserves those navy scrubs. Bailey & Richard: OGs 4ever DEADLINE: What about Grey’s veterans Chandra Wilson and James Pickens Jr.? Would Bailey’s plan for a degree in public health impact how much she will be on the show next season? And Richard had cancer. Are there any plans for him to scale back? Seems like he’s in every episode. MARINIS : He is in every episode. And those two are our OGs that are the pillars of the show. I do not envision a world where I can scale back on seeing either of them. Just due to the creative, we may be seeing Bailey in a different capacity, though. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ (L-R): Caterina Scorsone as Amelia, Jen Landon as Toni Disney/Anne Marie Fox Toni & Amelia: She Did What?! DEADLINE: You added Jen Landon as plastic surgeon Toni this season. We got this crazy cliffhanger with her and Amelia at the end that opens up two possibilities for Toni next season, her leaving after what happened or her being promoted to series regular. Which on e is it? MARINIS : Well, I love Jen Landon, and we were so lucky to get her and have her, and I think she really enjoyed her time here. Also, her character brings a really great side to Ben Warren, I love their working relationship. She’s this quirky plastic surgeon that we don’t really have a character like her anywhere else, and I would love to have her back. I don’t know if I would use the word promote, because we are in a different time in our industry with the budget, but I would love to have her come back as much as we can. DEADLINE: Speaking of the surprising cliffhanger, where did this seemingly random Amelia and Cass hookup come from? And what does it mean for Amelia and Toni who had just poured her heart out to her? MARINIS : I think Amelia truly felt like Toni was going back to her wife, and I think she was really sad about it. She had an emotional day with Meredith, and this pretty woman asked if she wanted to get coffee after a long day. I know it all happened off screen, but we love the surprise at the end. Obviously, Sophia Bush’s character is married, she’s in an open marriage, so I don’t think Sophia Bush’s character has left her husband or anything. I just think this is more of now Amelia has gotten herself into a little bit of trouble. I think she wants to be with Toni, and I think she was just trying to make herself feel better because she thought she had been rejected. And so, what we have to look for in the future is, can Toni overlook it? Does Amelia need to work her way back or do they have to work together and deny their chemistry while Toni’s repairing her feelings? We’ll just have to wait and see but they’re a great match. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ (L-R): Adelaide Kane as Jules, Anthony Hill as Winston Disney/Anne Marie Fox Winston & Jules: Dangerous Liaison DEADLINE: When we spoke about the power dynamic issue in the Winston and Jules relationship last year, you noted that a lot has changed since Meredith and Derek and that some things that were considered appropriate at the time are not anymore. Yet, you went with the storyline. Why? And what will the repercussions be of them being discovered by Ben? As Winston said when he professed his love to Jules, “I could be fired for everything I’m about to say.” MARINIS : Well, we didn’t see Ben tell Bailey, but you know that that’s going to happen at one point, so I think their little happy bubble will probably be popped, and I think that it’s just going to depend. I mean, Bailey, she’s married to someone who technically was a resident, so we’re just going to have to see how, if it’s hypocritical, for someone to say something. But I think people will have a lot to say about it once they find out that, yes, that was the cliffhanger of, oh no, now everything he was worried about could possibly happen. DEADLINE: But why did you decide to pursue that? And why did Winston do it? There was attraction…. MARINIS : They’re in love, Nellie. He couldn’t deny it. He tried so long. It was two seasons. DEADLINE: Okay, it’s Grey’s , love wins and trumps rules, I guess. MARINIS : But these days we have repercussions, so we’ll have to see what those are. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ Chris Carmack as Link Disney/Anne Marie Fox Jo & Link: Breaking Point DEADLINE: Jo is spiraling, she doesn’t even know if she wants to be any doctor anymore, let alone OB or surgeon. Is her internal crisis triggered by postpartum or is she genuinely not sure about her future? MARINIS : I think it’s a little bit in both. I think when you go through something like postpartum, there’s a little bit of I don’t know what my life should look like, what brings me happiness anymore and what brings me down? I think that it’s something that we really were interested in talking about a lot of times, our characters go through really big health scares, and then in two episodes, they moved along just fine. But I think in particular, especially with mothers and difficult deliveries, no one really talks about that, and it’s a disservice. And especially, just talking to so many people about maternal mortality, everyone always thinks, Oh, if the mom and the babies are saved, it’s a happy ending. Well, yes, it’s a happy ending, but you don’t know the emotional burden that people go through after. We heard from this doctor, and I said, this is too powerful a story not to tell and to let women know that it’s okay that you’re feeling like this. And I think, with the career aspect of it, her trigger is her job, because she’s seeing other women go through it. It’s just, can she maintain that or not? is the big question. DEADLINE: And you don’t have an answer right now? MARINIS: Not for you. DEADLINE: And Link, we’d seen from the beginning of the season where this was headed as he seems to be popping more and more painkillers. Is this going to escalate next season? MARINIS : Yes, we’ll definitely deal with the aftermath of this. He also went through such a big health scare at the beginning of this season, and he’s tried to power through the best he can for Jo. He’s someone who really prides himself on his strength and being there for his partner and his kids. And so I don’t think it’s an option for him to be weak and to not take care of them. We’ll have to look at that. When both members of a couple are going through something, it doesn’t necessarily mean that one person has to power through. It’s okay. I think we’re telling a different story about having to turn to medication to numb, I don’t think it’s going to look like the stereotypical abuse of medication that a lot of other shows and movies have done. I think it’s going to be more nuanced. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ (L-R): Niko Terho as Lucas, Alexis Floyd as Simone Disney/Anne Marie Fox Simone, Lucas & Wes: Three’s Company DEADLINE: Why did you decide to reignite the love triangle between Lucas, Simone and Wes with a big, classic Grey’s finale cliffhanger? MARINIS : Well, I think we put Lucas through it this season with his emotional patient story, Katie. And in that storyline, I think we saw him grow up a lot. I think we saw him grow as a doctor. And I also think Niko Terho had some of his best performances this year. He really went through it with Simone when Katie died. And for Simone, she definitely has feelings to sort out. Wes has been such a casual thing, and he stated that from the very beginning. And also, he’s an intern, she’s a second year, and I think she had always thought that this was just fun, I don’t think she ever thought it was necessarily going to be more than that. And then suddenly, when he’s opening up to her and the finale and saying, Would you want to hang out more?, It’s like, oh, this kind of throws her wrench, because it’s a great looking guy, and he’s clearly a hard working doctor, and you’ve got some pain that she’s seen a little bit about his brother. And then she thought that Lucas was just a one night thing, because that’s what they said, it was mistakes. I think she’s confused. I don’t think she thought both of these options were on the table. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’: Jade Pettyjohn as Dani Disney/Anne Marie Fox New Interns: We Barely Know You DEADLINE: Grey’s introduced a couple of new interns this season but none of them made an impression. Dani had a very memorable first day, but then kind of disappeared. There was a young guy who barely had a couple of lines, two lines. MARINIS : Harrison Meade, yeah. DEADLINE: Any any plans for them to come back? MARINIS : I’d love to see them come back. They really were fun characters to interact with ours. I think just in the last two episodes we had a lot of creative ground to cover with our regulars. title: ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ EP Meg Marinis On Season 23 Premiere’s Time Jump, Pregnancy Surprise, James Wolk’s Arrival & Doctor’s Exit; Texas Spinoff Status
full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Cupertino’ Creators Robert & Michelle King On Episode 2’s Shocking AGI Twist & Predicting The Future Again With AI Guardrails Storyline Netflix Shakeup: Peter Rice Is Welcomed Back To Executive Ranks While Bela Bajaria’s Exit Has Layoff-Weary Staff Bracing For More Upheaval ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ EP Meg Marinis On Season 23 Premiere’s Time Jump, Pregnancy Surprise, James Wolk’s Arrival & Doctor’s Exit; Texas Spinoff Status View All October 15, 2026 8:00pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source SPOILER ALERT: The story includes details about the Season 23 premiere of ABC’s Grey’s Anatomy. Time did not stand still at Grey Sloan as Grey’s Anatomy returned with its first time jump between seasons in four years. The Season 23 premiere picked up a month after the events in the Season 22 finale . It introduced the finished VIP floor and Seth Norton, played by new recurring cast member James Wolk , a handsome, arrogant surgeon-turned-businessman whose company Olympic Regent Health backed the luxury medical suite. His focus on the bottom line immediately clashed with Meredith’s ( Ellen Pompeo ) compassion, putting the two on a collision course as Norton was revealed at the end of the episode as Grey Sloan’s new Chief of Surgery, Teddy’s (Kim Raver) old job. Related Stories Books Chuck Lorre Q&A On The Care & Feeding Of Sitcom Stars & Why A WGA Strike Doomed Democracy News Ron Perlman Lines Up Hemingway Movie & Updates On 'Sons Of Anarchy' Spinoff 'Legends', That Third 'Hellboy' Film & Next Steps For His Asylm Studios There was no trace in the premiere of Nick (Scott Speedman) or mention of his engagement to Meredith in the S22 finale and no update on Teddy and Owen (Kevin McKidd) an their new life in France. Watch on Deadline At the end of last season, Simone (Alexis Floyd) was faced with Wes (Trevor Jackson) vs. Lucas (Niko Terho) dilemma after the former suggested making their casual relationship official and she had a drunken hookup with the latter. A month later, she is with Wes (and has a new hairstyle) but somehow cannot stop running into shirtless (and sometimes fully unclothed) Lucas. In one of the episode’s big twists, Simone discovered she is pregnant. Ben (Jason George) is still being a gentleman and has not ratted out Winston (Anthony Hill) to Bailey (Chandra Wilson) having a relationship with an intern, Jules (Adelaide Kane), giving Winston another chance to come clean himself. By the end of the premiere, Jules and Winston find themself in an even bigger predicament when Bailey, trying to delegate more so she can pursue a Masters degree, makes Winston residency director — and Jules’ direct boss. Kwan aka Blue (Harry Shum Jr.) is still fired and “self employed.” He returned secretly to Grey Sloan to save the life of his online French teacher with Simone’s help. Jo (Camilla Luddington) appeared fine and back at work but a coding patient triggered painful memories and, in the final seconds of the episode, she told Link (Chris Carmack) that she had quit her job. Just moments prior, Link had swiped some of Jo’s old pain meds as his addiction issues seem to only be getting bigger. Amelia’s (Caterina Scorsone) and Toni (Jen Landon)’s ongoing tension following Amelia’s dalliance with Cass (Sophia Bush) in the S22 finale blew up in a public fight over a patient’s care. The two ultimately reconciled and got back together. In an interview with Deadline, Grey’s Anatomy executive producer/showrunner Meg Marinis addressed the decision to introduce a time jump and a new antagonist played by Wolk as well as Pompeo and Scott Speedman’s availability, and broke down the episode’s biggest twists, including Simone’s pregnancy, Jo’s resignation, Toni & Amelia’s shenanigans, and Winston & Jules’ new dynamic. The Texas native also provided an update on the rural Texas-set spinoff she is co-creating with Grey’s Anatomy creator Shonda Rhimes, which has a straight-to-series order for midseason. DEADLINE: This was the first time jump since Grey’s introduced the new interns at the start of Season 22. Why did you decide to do it? MARINIS : It always allows a little bit more flexibility and storytelling, and I wanted to do something different, but also it allowed us to be able to creatively build that VIP floor, because obviously we didn’t see that VIP floor in the finale, and so yes, that is behind the decision-making. And also I didn’t know if I was going to be able to have Scott Speedman because of R.J. Decker , and we left him in a hospital bed, so that would have been a little bit tricky. DEADLINE: Scott’s Nick and Meredith got engaged in the Season 22 finale but she is not wearing a ring in the premiere. Is the engagement still on? It wasn’t even mentioned. MARINIS : Well, the engagement is still on. Meredith Grey has never really worn a ring, even when she was with Derek. So she’s not necessarily a ring wearer, but that’s not to say that once they get married they may have wedding bands. We’ll pick up that story though, don’t worry. DEADLINE: What does the Season 2 renewal of Scott’s show R.J. Decker mean in terms of his availability? Will you be able to have him on at all this season? MARINIS : Yes, we will see Nick. Obviously scheduling is always tricky, but good thing is it’s the same family with the show, so they help us out a little bit. But yeah, it’s tricky because they don’t shoot here, so it takes a bit of logistical magic, but yes, we’ll see him. [Both Grey’s and R.J. Decker are produced by 20th TV for ABC, filming in California and North Carolina, respectively.] James Wolk Disney/Ser Baffo DEADLINE: Was James Wolk’s character introduced because you knew you wouldn’t have Scott Speedman for long or did you just need to have another person in Meredith’s life? MARINIS : He was introduced as someone for the whole hospital, not necessarily just to play off of Meredith. He’s going to be the source of this conflict between this new floor and the rest of the hospital, and how our other characters play off of that. In particular, we’ll see Richard and how he feels about working side by side with someone who doesn’t really know… That’s the craziest thing, we haven’t had a chief like this who isn’t part of the hospital to begin with, so he’s essentially a stranger to a lot of our people, and he may not see the interpersonal dynamics that everybody else has. DEADLINE: But Seth and Meredith will continue to interact, even if it’s not romantic, right? There was something about them together in the premiere . MARINIS : You’ll see them together again. Nick is the romantic partner but it’s always nice to, I feel like Meredith fights all of our battles for us. She’s the one that always says the thing that we’re always thinking but can’t say, and so we’ll see her say some of that to Seth. DEADLINE: And Nick is fully recovered after the accident, right? MARINIS : He’s doing great. DEADLINE: Meredith was in the premiere before leaving for Boston. How many episodes is Ellen in this season? MARINIS : We don’t have an exact number because we always need to wait to see how our schedule is. But don’t worry, that’s not the last you’ve seen her. You’ll see her several times. MIA Doctors: Teddy, Owen & Kwan DEADLINE: There was only a fleeting reference to Teddy and Owen in the premiere as Winston complained that he has to pick up their cases but no mention how th ey’re doing in France. MARINIS : Because it’s been a month in story time, I think it’s a little odd to keep talking about them, but man, do we miss them? And I miss the actors too. It does feel like there are missing doctors in the hospital, and I did not want for the hospital to seem like they replaced them already, so that’s kind of what Winston is talking about, he’s having to cover for them, and it’s wreaking havoc. DEADLINE: Speaking of missing doctors, Kwan is still fired a month later. He said he’s self-employed in the French class. What is he doing as self-employed? MARINIS : He was just saying that to cover himself with his class. But no, he’s unemployed, and I think he’s a little bit in denial and saying that he likes being unemployed, but we know that’s not real. He definitely misses it. DEADLINE: How has it been sharing Shum Jr. with Dancing ? Did you have to reduce his presence on Grey’s this season? MARINIS : No, we didn’t have to reduce his presence at all. We haven’t adjusted creative yet because Blue is such an important part of the show. Obviously, it can get tricky scheduling, but we knew about this going into it, we had everything on the table at the start of the season. We know which day and a half that they always need him, and we’ve been able to make it work. He’s practicing here, he’s rehearsing outside the stages with his partner. He will tape [Dancing] on Tuesday night and be here at 6:15 the next morning. DEADLINE: Aren’t you concerned that Shum Jr.’s Dancing video packages showing him wearing scrubs on the hospital set of Grey’s spoiled any suspence over Blue’s firing, revealing that he will be back at Grey Sloan? MARINIS : I feel like after watching the premiere, people will know that somehow he’s going to get folded back in. It’s the how is what we’ll discover. DEADLINE : Any chance of Harry dancing on Grey’s? MARINIS : Well, now you know I’m gonna want it. Alexis Floyd, Trevor Jackson, Harry Shum Jr. Disney/Raymond Liu Who’s the Daddy? DEADLINE: Simone’s surprise pregnancy. We saw Wes and Simone in the premiere being careful about condom use. Does that automatically mean Lucas is the dad because he and Simone’s hookup was unplanned or are we going to have another Who’s the daddy mystery like the one with Amelia’s baby? MARINIS : It does not automatically mean it is Lucas. It is a big old question, and it’s messy, and I guess yes, we did it with Amelia, but this is just as fun, and it’s going to play out differently. She’s an amazing surgeon, but when it comes to her personal life, Simone’s a little bit messy. DEADLINE: So we won’t find out right away, the mystery will carry on for awhile? MARINIS : Yeah, I don’t know how you find out. DEADLINE: Simone can count the dates, I guess. MARINIS : It was all happening at once, so it’s pretty tricky. Jen Landon, Chris Carmack, Camilla Luddington Disney/Ser Baffo Jo’s Relapse DEADLINE: I’m glad that you did a course correction on Jo because she seemed too well adjusted at the start of the premiere for someone who was spiraling post-trauma a month ago. We saw that all unravel after she watched a patient being cut open. Was that the trigger for her? MARINIS : We’ll come to understand more specifically in later episodes what her actual triggers are, but, after suffering an almost death experience, when she sees other people doing the same, for me that is that is a trigger. Obviously that person, their chest was cut open, her chest was cut open, so she has that same exact scar, things like that. I just think that it’s seeing people at that pivotal point of, if they’re going to make it or not make it, that coding experience. That elevator was definitely a trigger. DEADLINE: Was Jo quitting just an emotional reaction to a bad day at the hospital that she would overcome or will it play out longer with her staying away from Grey Sloan? MARINIS : It will, being at the hospital in a regular employed fashion, she won’t be there. I mean, she might be at the hospital, but not working shifts every day like she was in the past. This definitely plays out. It’s not in Episode 2, she’s back in scrubs. DEADLINE: Is this a similar situation to when Amelia took a sabbatical after another traumatic experience at Grey Sloan that translated into Caterina going an an extended hiatus . Will Camilla be in fewer episodes this season? MARINIS : No, that is not the situation. This is a creative decision where we wanted to play the reality of what Jo went through, and you’ll see the impact of that on her not being at work, and whether or not she regrets the decision or whether she’s reaffirmed in the decision, we’ll that play out. DEADLINE: So nobody will have significantly reduced episodes this year, right? MARINIS : We always have to kind of wait and see, but right now things are looking fairly normal. DEADLINE: With Jo sidelined, Kwan fired and Teddy and Owen in France, the hospital is four doctors down. Are you planning any other major additions to Grey Sloan’s medical/surgical staff this season besides James’ Seth and Jen’s Toni? MARINIS : No, James Wolk and Jen Landon are our recurring guest surgeons right now. Caterina Scorsone, Jen Landon Disney/Raymond Liu Amelia & Toni Kiss and Make Up DEADLINE: Jen’s Toni and Amelia had a happy ending in the premiere after the heartbreaker of the finale. Yes, a month passed but I feel like you got them back together a little too qu ickly . MARINIS : I need joy, Nellie. DEADLINE: I think Toni was very forgiving, one short speech by Amelia, and that’s all it took. MARINIS : Well, it’s so funny. It was such a debate in the writers room because we were like, oh my gosh, Amelia slept with somebody else, Toni can’t forgive her. But then, Toni was kind of toying with her at the end there, am I going to get back together with my ex, am I not going to get back together with my ex? It’s not that Amelia went into that to cheat on her, it was she was trying to dull the pain that she felt that Toni was going with her ex-wife, and so it’s a bit of a misunderstanding. They’re just so great for each other, and I think also, when you lose a patient together, things change. We’ll see if they can stay happy or not as the episodes play out, but I really love them as a couple, they have great chemistry. DEADLINE: They lost a patient but I’m not sure if they didn’t contribute to that with their fight in the OR over treatment that may have proven costly. It was highly inappropriate too, in front of their colleagues, that was not the place for that. MARINIS : No, of course not. But that’s what Grey’s is, right? We bring our problems to work. DEADLINE: BTW, we saw Toni fly back in the premiere. Was she gone from Seattle for the entire month after the finale? MARINIS : I don’t know if she left immediately right after the finale, but she’s been gone for at least a few weeks. Winston & Jules Cross New Line DEADLINE: Winston and Jules’ relationship for me has always been crossing a line. But the show is now creating a new obstacle that makes it very, very problematic with Winston appointed residency director. How will that impact them? MARINIS : We’re definitely going to play that out so you’re going to see where that goes immediately with Episode 2, how they have to navigate this new dynamic with him being her direct supervisor. And you’re right, it is now like, we crossed the line, and now we’re looking back, waving at it. It’s putting a whole other layer on it, whether or not they can stay together, and if they do stay together, how do they come forward? It’s going to be messy, and there’s going to be conflict, and they might not agree on it. Jason George, Chandra Wilson, Anthony Hill Disney/Ser Baffo DEADLINE: How about Ben, keeping Winston and Jules’ secret for a month? Is that a moot point now or is it a Chekhov’s Gun situation where the gun (aka the secret) hangs on the wall for awhile until it eventually goes off? MARINIS : It’s that one. Texas Spinoff Status Update DEADLINE: What is the status of the Grey’s Anatomy Texas spinoff? There has been casting chatter, and I heard start of production was pushed from fall to January. How is it shaping up, and are you currently casting? MARINIS : We are currently working hard on it. I’m just grateful that I get to create this with Shonda, it’s a dream. We’re working hard, and we’re working away, and I’m learning a lot about developing and creating a show, which I didn’t know before. I can’t release anything yet on timing, but I’m excited for y’all to see it. DEADLINE: How is it doing it with Shonda? MARINIS : Oh, it’s amazing. It’s one thing to be able to work for her but to be able to do it with her it’s really fun. She spins everything into gold; you send something to her and then she sends it back and it’s amazing. It’s really fun, I haven’t been able to work like this with her in a while, she’s branched out and gotten so many shows, so it’s it’s really fun. We have a great relationship. DEADLINE: We are going to see characters from the spinoff on Grey’s this season, right? MARINIS : We’re still figuring out which episode, but yeah, just, traditionally with a spinoff [that’s done]. We’re still working out on timing. Season 23 Theme & Possible Returns DEADLINE: What is the theme of Season 23? Is it about concierge medicine and money’s role in medicine overall? MARINIS : It’s related to that, but honestly, I’ve been looking at identity as a theme, and that’s being reflected in that concierge floor. People have very different opinions on it, on how to treat patients and what kind of doctors they’re going to be, so it’s really about identity and when the world is in a state of rapid change, do you change with it or do you stay true to yourself? I feel like a lot of the stories this season involve our characters being in one spot while the world is just furiously spinning around us, which I think we all have a little bit of experience in right now. Whether it’s AI, whether it’s climate, things are happening so quickly. It’s really hard to know what day it is. DEADLINE: Any chance of Kim Raver or Kevin McKidd coming back for a visit? Or any other former cast members? There were not that many alum returns last season and none in the premiere. MARINIS : We’re always open to bringing back old characters. One of the joys of having a Season 23 show is that you get to do that, and it’s also such a great gift to the fans. It always just depends on how much room we have creatively and people’s schedules because people leave the show and they go on to take other jobs, and it just gets tricky. But I’m always keeping my eye on ways to introduce people to come back for a show or two. DEADLINE: Any plans to make this the final season of Grey’s ? MARINIS : Oh my gosh, no one’s told me that, so I’m gonna keep on doing what I’m doing.
